titleEn: Caramelized Baked Rice Pudding
description: A creamy Turkish milk-and-rice pudding baked in individual dishes until the surface blisters and caramelizes.

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.substitute: Whole milk; replace up to 1 cup with half-and-half for extra richness.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.substitute: Potato starch, using the same amount.

ingredients.name: Egg yolk
ingredients.substitute: Omit for an egg-free version; pudding will be slightly less rich.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Simmer it with the water in a saucepan until very soft and most water is absorbed.
Add milk and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring often so the milk does not scorch.
Whisk cornstarch and egg yolk with a ladle of hot pudding until smooth, then stir back into the pot. Simmer until lightly thickened; stir in vanilla.
Divide among six shallow oven-safe ramekins. Set them in a roasting pan and pour hot water into the pan halfway up the sides.
Broil on high, watching closely, until the tops are deeply spotted and caramelized. Cool, then chill before serving.

titleEn: Pistachio Baklava
description: Paper-thin layers of buttery phyllo enclose finely chopped pistachios, finished with fragrant lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: Frozen phyllo dough, thawed
ingredients.substitute: Greek filo pastry from the freezer section; thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

ingredients.name: Shelled unsalted pistachios
ingredients.substitute: Raw unsalted California pistachios, finely chopped; Turkish Antep pistachios are ideal if available.

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.substitute: A thin strip of lemon peel plus a little bottled lemon juice.

steps.instruction: Make syrup by simmering sugar and water until clear. Add lemon juice and optional rose water, then cool completely.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush a 9-by-13-inch baking pan with butter. Keep phyllo covered with a barely damp towel as you work.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in the pan, brushing each lightly with butter. Scatter pistachios evenly over the layers.
Layer the remaining phyllo on top, buttering each sheet. Cut into diamonds or squares with a sharp knife before baking.
Bake until crisp and deeply golden. Immediately pour the cool syrup evenly over the hot baklava. Let stand until syrup is absorbed and pastry is fully cooled.

titleEn: Cheese-Filled Crispy Shredded Pastry
description: Golden, crisp strands of kataifi surround stretchy unsalted cheese and are soaked with lemon syrup while hot.

ingredients.name: Frozen kataifi shredded pastry, thawed
ingredients.substitute: Frozen Greek kataifi pastry from Mediterranean markets or online.

ingredients.name: Unsalted melting cheese
ingredients.substitute: A mix of low-moisture mozzarella and mild provolone; traditional künefe cheese is best when available.

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.substitute: Fresh lime juice in a pinch.

steps.instruction: Simmer sugar and water for 8–10 minutes. Stir in lemon juice and keep the syrup warm.
Separate kataifi strands with your fingers and mix thoroughly with melted butter. Press half into a buttered 10-inch oven-safe skillet.
Spread grated cheese evenly over the pastry, leaving a small border. Cover with remaining buttered kataifi and press firmly.
Cook over medium-low heat until the underside is crisp and golden, then carefully flip using a plate and cook the other side until the cheese melts.
Pour warm syrup over the hot künefe, garnish with pistachios, and serve immediately while the cheese is stretchy.

titleEn: Citrus Semolina Syrup Cake
description: A tender semolina cake scented with citrus and soaked in light lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: Fine semolina
ingredients.substitute: Coarse durum wheat semolina or coarse farina.

ingredients.name: Plain whole-milk yogurt
ingredients.substitute: Greek yogurt loosened with 1–2 tbsp milk.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.substitute: Use a commercial egg replacer for baking, following its package directions.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil
ingredients.substitute: Mild olive oil or melted butter.

steps.instruction: For the syrup, simmer 1 cup sugar with 1½ cups water and 1 tbsp lemon juice until dissolved. Let cool.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in yogurt, oil, and lemon zest.
Fold in semolina, flour, and baking powder. Spread batter in a greased 9-by-13-inch pan.
Bake until golden and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cut the warm cake into squares and slowly pour the cooled syrup over it. Rest until the syrup is absorbed before serving.

titleEn: Almond Semolina Cookies in Syrup
description: Soft, buttery semolina cookies are baked golden, topped with almonds, and soaked in lemon syrup.

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.substitute: Commercial egg replacer suitable for cookies.

steps.instruction: Simmer 1½ cups sugar with 2 cups water for 10 minutes. Add 1 tsp lemon juice and cool the syrup completely.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Cream butter and powdered sugar, then beat in eggs. Mix in flour, semolina, and baking powder to form a soft dough.
Shape into 20 oval cookies, arrange on a lined baking sheet, and press an almond into each center.
Bake until the cookies are lightly golden on top and golden underneath.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cookies in their pan. Let stand until syrup is absorbed and cookies are tender.

titleEn: Caramelized Milk Pudding
description: A silky milk pudding with a signature toasted, caramelized underside, chilled and rolled for serving.

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.substitute: Whole milk; half-and-half may replace 1 cup for richer flavor.

ingredients.name: Unsalted butter
ingredients.substitute: Neutral oil for greasing the pan.

steps.instruction: Whisk rice flour and cornstarch with 1 cup of the cold milk until smooth.
Heat remaining milk and sugar in a heavy saucepan. Whisk in the starch mixture and cook, stirring constantly, until very thick and glossy.
Lightly butter a wide nonstick pan or metal tray. Sprinkle a thin layer of sugar over the base and heat gently until it melts and turns amber.
Spread the hot pudding over the caramelized base. Cook over low heat until the bottom is toasted in patches, taking care not to burn it.
Cool, then refrigerate until completely set. Cut into strips and roll with the caramelized side outward.

titleEn: Buttery Semolina Halva with Pine Nuts
description: Nutty semolina slowly toasted in butter, then steamed with warm sweet milk and pine nuts.

ingredients.name: Coarse semolina
ingredients.substitute: Coarse durum wheat semolina or coarse farina.

ingredients.name: Whole milk
ingredients.substitute: Water or half milk and half water.

steps.instruction: Warm milk with sugar in a small saucepan until the sugar dissolves; keep warm but do not boil.
Melt butter in a heavy saucepan. Add pine nuts and semolina and toast over low-medium heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant and golden tan.
Carefully pour in the warm milk mixture; it will steam vigorously. Stir until combined.
Cover and cook over very low heat until the liquid is absorbed. Turn off heat and leave covered to steam.
Fluff gently with a fork, rest briefly, and serve warm with cinnamon if desired.

titleEn: Poached Quince with Clotted Cream
description: Quince halves slowly poached in sugar syrup until ruby-pink and tender, served cool with rich cream.

ingredients.name: Large quinces
ingredients.substitute: Firm pears, though they will cook faster and have a milder flavor.

ingredients.name: Kaymak-style cream
ingredients.substitute: Italian mascarpone or Devon English clotted cream.

steps.instruction: Peel and halve the quinces, remove cores, and rub cut surfaces with lemon juice to limit browning. Reserve the seeds in a tea infuser or tied cheesecloth for color and pectin.
Arrange quince halves cut-side up in a wide pot. Add water, sugar, cloves, lemon juice, and reserved seeds.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and poach until a knife slides easily into the fruit, turning pieces once if needed.
Uncover and simmer gently until the syrup thickens and the quince turns a deep pink-red. Cool in the syrup.
Serve at room temperature or chilled with a spoonful of mascarpone or clotted cream and chopped walnuts.

titleEn: Candied Squash with Tahini and Walnuts
description: Tender, glossy pumpkin or winter squash pieces cooked in sugar and finished with nutty tahini and crunchy walnuts.

ingredients.name: Peeled pumpkin or butternut squash
ingredients.substitute: Butternut squash is widely available and holds its shape well.

ingredients.name: Tahini
ingredients.substitute: Smooth sesame paste; almond butter is a different-flavored alternative.

steps.instruction: Cut squash into 2-inch chunks and arrange in a wide heavy pot in one layer. Sprinkle sugar evenly over the pieces.
Cover and leave at room temperature until the squash releases juice and the sugar becomes wet.
Set over low heat, covered, and cook gently in its own syrup until the squash is tender but still holds its shape.
Uncover and simmer until the syrup is glossy and slightly reduced. Cool in the pot.
Arrange on a platter, drizzle with tahini, and scatter with walnuts and optional cinnamon.

titleEn: Baked Shredded Pastry with Walnuts
description: Crisp, buttery strands of shredded pastry layered with walnuts and soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup.

ingredients.name: Frozen kataifi shredded pastry, thawed
ingredients.substitute: Frozen Greek kataifi from Mediterranean markets or online.

steps.instruction: Simmer sugar and water for 10 minutes, stir in lemon juice, then cool the syrup completely.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C). Pull kataifi strands apart and toss thoroughly with melted butter.
Press half the pastry into a buttered 9-by-13-inch pan, distribute walnuts evenly, and cover with remaining pastry. Press gently.
Bake until deeply golden and crisp across the surface.
Pour cool syrup evenly over the hot pastry. Leave to absorb and cool before cutting into squares.

titleEn: Turkish Chocolate Mosaic Cake
description: A no-bake refrigerator cake made from broken tea biscuits bound with a cocoa-chocolate mixture and sliced to reveal a mosaic.

ingredients.name: Plain tea biscuits
ingredients.substitute: Petite beurre, Maria, or plain digestive biscuits.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened cocoa powder
ingredients.substitute: Dutch-process cocoa for a smoother flavor.

steps.instruction: Break biscuits into bite-size pieces in a large bowl, keeping some larger chunks for the mosaic pattern.
Gently heat butter, milk, sugar, cocoa, and chopped chocolate in a saucepan, stirring until smooth. Do not boil.
Cool the chocolate mixture for a few minutes, then fold it through the biscuits and optional nuts until evenly coated.
Spoon onto parchment or plastic wrap and shape into a firm log or press into a loaf pan. Cover tightly.
Refrigerate until firm, then slice with a warm knife and serve cold.

titleEn: Crispy Turkish Sweet Fritters in Lemon Syrup
description: Small yeast-raised dough balls fried until crisp and dipped in cool lemon syrup for a crunchy, airy center.

steps.instruction: Simmer 1½ cups sugar with 1 cup water for 8–10 minutes. Add lemon juice and cool completely.
Mix flour, yeast, sugar, and warm water into a sticky, stretchy batter. Cover and leave in a warm place until bubbly and expanded.
Heat oil in a deep heavy pot to 350°F (175°C). Working in small batches, drop teaspoon-size portions of batter into the oil.
Fry, turning, until puffed and evenly deep golden. Transfer briefly to a rack or paper towel.
Dip hot fritters into cool syrup for about 30–60 seconds, then serve while crisp.

titleEn: Traditional Noah's Pudding
description: A festive, fruit- and grain-rich pudding combining wheat, beans, chickpeas, dried fruit, and nuts, served with traditional toppings.

ingredients.name: Shelled whole wheat berries
ingredients.substitute: Pearled wheat or hulled barley; texture will differ slightly.

ingredients.name: Cooked white beans, drained
ingredients.substitute: Canned cannellini or navy beans, rinsed well.

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.substitute: Adjust to taste depending on dried fruit sweetness.

ingredients.name: Pomegranate seeds and chopped nuts for topping
ingredients.substitute: Cinnamon, walnuts, hazelnuts, or dried coconut.

steps.instruction: Soak wheat berries overnight. Drain, cover with fresh water, and simmer until very tender, adding water as needed.
Add cooked chickpeas and white beans to the tender wheat. Simmer gently, stirring occasionally.
Add diced apricots, raisins, orange zest, and sugar. Add hot water as needed for a loose pudding consistency.
Taste and adjust sweetness. Simmer until fruit softens and flavors meld; stir carefully to prevent sticking.
Ladle into bowls. Cool, then garnish with pomegranate seeds, chopped nuts, and cinnamon before serving.

titleEn: Rich Chocolate Pudding with Cake Center
description: A glossy Turkish chocolate pudding enriched with dark chocolate and butter, spooned over a small piece of cake in each bowl.

ingredients.name: All-purpose flour
ingredients.substitute: Cornstarch, using about 3 tbsp, for a glossier texture.

ingredients.name: Plain sponge cake
ingredients.substitute: Ladyfingers or simple pound cake cut into cubes.

steps.instruction: Whisk sugar, flour, cornstarch, and cocoa in a saucepan. Gradually whisk in cold milk until smooth.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until the pudding thickens and bubbles gently.
Remove from heat. Stir in chopped chocolate and butter until completely melted and glossy.
Place a piece of sponge cake in each serving glass or bowl. Pour the hot pudding over the cake.
Cool briefly, cover, and refrigerate until chilled and set. Serve plain or with grated chocolate.

titleEn: Syrup-Soaked Cheese Pastry Balls
description: Small cheese-based pastry balls simmered in sugar syrup until tender and saturated, traditionally served chilled.

ingredients.name: Kemalpaşa dessert cheese balls, dried or packaged
ingredients.substitute: If unavailable, use small baked ricotta dumplings made from ricotta, egg, flour, and semolina; texture will vary.

ingredients.name: Lemon juice
ingredients.substitute: A small strip of lemon peel.

ingredients.name: Kaymak-style cream (optional)
ingredients.substitute: Mascarpone or Devon English clotted cream.

steps.instruction: Combine sugar and water in a wide saucepan and bring to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add lemon juice.
Add the dried Kemalpaşa balls carefully to the simmering syrup, leaving room for them to expand.
Simmer gently, turning the balls occasionally, until they swell and become tender and translucent around the edges. Follow package timing if supplied.
Remove from heat and let the pastries cool in the syrup so they absorb more sweetness.
Serve chilled or at room temperature with optional mascarpone or clotted cream and chopped pistachios.

titleEn: Balkan Caramel Three-Milk Sponge Cake (Trileçe)
description: Feather-light airy sponge cake soaked in a chilled trinity of condensed milk, whole milk, and heavy cream, crowned with a glossy amber ribbon of homemade caramelized sugar.

ingredients.name: Whole Milk & Heavy Cream Blend (for soaking)
ingredients.substitute: 3 cups whole milk and 1 cup heavy whipping cream with 2 tbsp sugar

ingredients.name: Amber Caramel Sauce
ingredients.substitute: Dulce de leche or homemade cooked caramel

steps.instruction: Beat egg whites with half the sugar until stiff peaks form. Beat yolks with remaining sugar until pale; fold gently with flour and baking powder.
Bake sponge in a greased glass baking dish at 340°F (170°C) until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Poke holes across warm cake with a skewer. Whisk cold milk, cream, and sugar; pour evenly over the cake until fully absorbed. Chill.
Pour smooth caramel sauce over the chilled cake, score traditional chevron lines with cream, and slice into generous squares.

titleEn: Traditional Ramadan Milk and Pomegranate Dessert (Güllaç)
description: Ottoman Ramadan masterwork crafted with crisp cornstarch wafers softened in sweetened warm rosewater milk, layered with toasted walnuts and adorned with ruby pomegranate arils and emerald pistachios.

ingredients.name: Dry Güllaç Sheets (Cornstarch wafers)
ingredients.substitute: Rice paper sheets (thin) or delicate wafer sheets

steps.instruction: Heat milk and sugar in a pot until warm to the touch (110°F / 45°C, not boiling). Stir in rosewater.
Lay half the güllaç sheets shiny-side up in a large deep tray, ladling warm milk over each sheet until soaked and pliable.
Scatter chopped walnuts evenly across the center layer. Cover with remaining sheets, ladling milk over each.
Chill in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours. Garnish each square with pomegranate seeds and pistachios before serving.

titleEn: Ridged Semolina Cookies with Walnuts in Syrup (Kalburabastı)
description: Rustic Anatolian festive dessert pressed over a sieve grater to create its signature honeycomb ridges, stuffed with toasted walnuts and soaked in fragrant lemon syrup until meltingly tender.

steps.instruction: Boil 3 cups sugar and 3 cups water with lemon juice for 15 minutes to create syrup; cool completely.
Knead butter, olive oil, yogurt, egg, semolina, flour, and baking soda into a soft pliable dough.
Flatten walnut-sized balls of dough onto a textured sieve or grater. Place walnuts in center, seal edges, and peel off to preserve textured pattern.
Bake seam-side down at 375°F (190°C) until deep golden. Pour cold syrup over hot cookies immediately.

titleEn: Crispy Golden Fluted Fritters in Syrup (Tulumba)
description: Beloved Turkish street dessert of choux-like piped fluted dough fried in oil until audibly crackling and instantly dunked into ice-cold fragrant lemon sugar syrup.

steps.instruction: Boil water with butter; stir in flour all at once and cook vigorously until a smooth ball pulls away from the sides. Cool.
Beat in eggs one by one along with semolina and cornstarch until shiny and smooth.
Pipe 2-inch fluted cylinders with a star nozzle into cool/lukewarm oil using oiled kitchen scissors.
Fry over medium heat, stirring gently until crisp and chestnut brown, then plunge directly into ice-cold syrup.

titleEn: Clotted Cream and Pistachio Filo Triangles (Şöbiyet)
description: Crown jewel of Turkish baklava houses: delicate diamond-folded parcels of 30 gossamer filo sheets stuffed with semolina clotted cream and ground Antep pistachios, baked in clarified butter.

steps.instruction: Cook 2 cups milk with 4 tbsp semolina until thick; cool completely into firm pudding kaymak.
Layer filo sheets, brushing lightly with clarified butter. Cut the stack into 3-inch squares.
Place a dollop of semolina cream and a spoonful of ground pistachios in the center; fold into triangles.
Arrange overlapping in a buttered pan, pour remaining hot clarified butter over, and bake at 380°F (190°C) until puffed and golden. Douse in warm syrup.

titleEn: Pure Pistachio Marzipan Roll (Fıstık Sarma)
description: Vibrant emerald green Gaziantep delicacy crafted from a single paper-thin sheet of filo rolled tightly around an unadulterated center of pure ground Antep pistachios and light syrup.

ingredients.name: Antep Emerald Green Pistachio Powder
ingredients.substitute: First-harvest early crop Turkish green pistachios

steps.instruction: Lay one sheet of fresh baklava filo on marble. Sprinkle a thick, solid carpet of bright green pistachio powder edge-to-edge.
Roll using a thin rolling pin (oklava) into a slender tight cigar rope.
Gently push from both ends to crinkle slightly, slide onto a baking tray, and slice into 2-inch segments.
Brush with clarified butter and bake gently at 320°F (160°C) so it stays vivid green without browning. Soak in light syrup.

titleEn: Real Ottoman Shredded Chicken Breast Pudding (Tavukgöğsü)
description: Ancient Ottoman court pudding prepared with real chicken breast boiled, pounded, and teased into micro-filaments, cooked with whole milk and rice flour into a silky, stringy elastic dessert dusted with cinnamon.

steps.instruction: Boil chicken breast until tender. Soak in cold water, changing water frequently to remove any chicken scent, then shred by hand into hair-thin threads.
Pound shredded chicken threads in a mortar with a splash of milk until fibers separate completely.
Simmer milk, sugar, rice flour, and starch until thickened. Add chicken fibers and beat continuously with a wooden spoon until stringy and chewy.
Pour into a shallow dish, chill overnight, roll into cylinders, and dust generously with ground cinnamon.

titleEn: Fermented Dried Fig and Warm Milk Pudding (İncir Uyutması)
description: Magic Aegean natural dessert made without added sugar or gelatin: dried Aegean figs steeped in warm milk and pureed, wrapped in blankets to 'sleep' (ferment naturally) until setting like silk.

ingredients.name: Whole Milk (warm, not boiling - yogurt temperature)

steps.instruction: Soak dried figs in warm water for 15 minutes, remove stems, and chop finely.
Heat milk to 115°F (46°C, just warm enough to hold a finger). Add chopped figs and purée with an immersion blender until smooth.
Pour into individual serving bowls. Cover with a tray and wrap tightly in thick blankets/towels to 'sleep' undisturbed.
Uncover once set like pudding; chill in the fridge and garnish with toasted walnuts.

titleEn: Lips of the Beauty Folded Pastry in Syrup (Dilber Dudağı)
description: Ottoman layered pastry rolled with cornstarch into dozens of flaky layers, cut into round discs, folded like lip petals over a toasted walnut center, and drenched in sweet lemon syrup.

steps.instruction: Knead dough, divide into 10 balls. Roll each ball thin with cornstarch, stack, and roll the stack together into one large sheet.
Cut circles with a glass rim. Place walnut pieces in center and fold gently like a half-moon lip without pressing edges.
Arrange on a baking sheet, pour hot melted butter over, and bake at 375°F (190°C) until leaves open and turn golden.
Pour cold syrup over hot pastries immediately.

titleEn: Izmir Street-Style Semolina Cake with Peanuts (Şambali)
description: Dense, chewy, flourless semolina street cake from Izmir made with yogurt, molasses, and baking soda, decorated with blanched peanut rows, baked until dark caramelized brown, and soaked in thick syrup.

steps.instruction: Mix coarse semolina, sugar, yogurt, and baking soda into a thick batter; rest for 2 hours so semolina plumps.
Brush a metal baking tray with grape molasses and water. Press batter evenly 1-inch thick; score rectangular bars.
Press a halved peanut into each bar. Bake at 360°F (180°C) until deeply caramelized and brown.
Pour boiling syrup over warm cake; rest overnight for maximum chewy texture.

titleEn: Lady's Navel Fried Choux Pastry in Syrup (Hanım Göbeği)
description: Ottoman palace dessert of golden choux pastry rings indented in the center to resemble a navel, gently fried in warm oil until puffed and crisp, soaked in fragrant lemon syrup.

steps.instruction: Cook water and butter with flour until a ball forms; cool, then incorporate eggs one by one.
Roll walnut-sized balls with oiled hands, flatten slightly, and press a deep dent into the center with an oiled thumb.
Drop into cool oil, slowly raise heat, and fry until puffed double in size and golden brown.
Drop directly into cold syrup; soak for 15 minutes and garnish with pistachios.

titleEn: Nightingale's Nest Rolled Pistachio Filo (Bülbül Yuvası)
description: Baklava sheets rolled around an oklava rolling pin, crinkled and curled into individual round nest cups, filled to the brim with whole Antep pistachios, and baked to amber crispness in clarified butter.

steps.instruction: Brush filo sheet with butter, roll loosely onto a thin wooden pin, accordion-wrinkle from both ends, and slide off.
Curl the ruffled rope into a circular nest, bringing ends together and tucking base inside.
Pack the center of each nest with whole pistachios, pour remaining clarified butter over all nests.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) until crispy and golden; pour warm syrup over hot nests.

titleEn: Erzurum Deep-Fried Shredded Pastry Rolls with Walnuts (Kadayıf Dolması)
description: Erzurum masterpiece of fresh shredded kadayıf threads rolled tightly around toasted walnuts into plump cigars, dipped in whisked eggs, deep-fried until crackling, and dipped into cold lemon syrup.

steps.instruction: Spread a palm-sized bundle of fresh kadayıf strands onto a board. Place walnuts at the end and roll tightly into a cylinder.
Briefly coat each roll in beaten eggs, shaking off excess with hands.
Deep fry in hot oil (360°F / 180°C) until deep amber brown and crunchy.
Plunge directly into cold syrup for 5 minutes; serve warm with clotted cream kaymak.

titleEn: Vizier's Finger Semolina Pastries in Syrup (Vezir Parmağı)
description: Ottoman finger-shaped soft semolina pastries rolled in semolina for a crunchy exterior texture, baked golden and soaked in aromatic lemon-scented sugar syrup.

steps.instruction: Knead butter, egg, yogurt, oil, flour, semolina, and baking powder into a tender dough.
Roll dough pieces into finger-length cylinders (about 3 inches long). Roll each in dry semolina to coat.
Bake on a greased sheet at 375°F (190°C) until golden brown.
Pour cold syrup over hot pastries and let rest until plump and moist.

titleEn: Ottoman Palace Saffron and Rice Jelly Pudding (Zerde)
description: Dazzling golden celebration dessert of the Ottoman palace: broken rice simmered in water with saffron threads and turmeric, sweetened with rosewater and decorated with currants, pine nuts, and pomegranate seeds.

ingredients.name: Pine Nuts, Dried Currants & Pomegranate Arils

steps.instruction: Steep saffron threads in 2 tbsp warm rosewater for 20 minutes to extract vibrant color and aroma.
Boil rice in 5 cups water until grains are completely soft and translucent.
Add sugar, saffron rosewater infusion, and turmeric; stir in dissolved cornstarch and simmer until glossy and thickened.
Ladle into glass bowls, chill until set, and decorate with currants, toasted pine nuts, and pomegranate seeds.
